accompanying_remediation: The four empty responses already in the cache are evicted, originals preserved byte-for-byte, and the terminal-halt records naming their cells are superseded so those cells are retried rather than permanently excluded. Without this the fix would prevent new losses while leaving the three already incurred.
archive_continuity: The run continues in the same archive. The call cache is seeded from genesis rather than from the execution identity, so an identity change does not invalidate it, and the supersession is recorded in the archive's ledger binding rather than rewritten. Same pattern the 2026-07-28 canary used three times.
bounds_retained: checker_unresolved remains terminal: that is the checker answering in a way the parser reads but cannot act on, which at temperature 0 is what it will answer again.
the same-call limit is unchanged, so a checker that keeps returning nothing for one specific call is still a deterministic failure that reaches a human.
a non-empty but unparseable response is still cached and still halts; only the empty case changed.
note: Append-only. Records the basis for an authorization.
subject: bridge canary, continuing in place, with empty checker responses no longer cached
the_one_change: rejudge/phase2_caching_client.py no longer memoises a response that is empty or whitespace only. Nothing else in the code bundle moved.

why.cost_if_unchanged: roughly 116 unrecoverable cells over the 23,200-cell main run, each stopping the supervisor for manual handling, and a bridge canary that could not hold a window open long enough to measure whether gemma tolerates concurrency at all.
why.measured: 4 empty checker responses in 205 calls (1.95%) against a 0.6% frozen tolerance; 3 terminal halts in 598 cells, one per ~199.
why.mechanism: an empty response is the absence of an answer, not a slow one. Caching it made every resume replay the same unreadable response, so the cell could never complete: a transient converted into a permanent.

why_this_is_not_retry_until_favourable: The frozen checker runs at temperature 0 (decisions.execution_semantics.temperature_by_call_role.query_checker), so a successful call is DETERMINISTIC. Re-calling recovers the decision the failed call should have returned; it does not draw a fresh sample, and there is no distribution of answers to select from. The frozen semantic_retry_policy ('never regenerate an invalid verdict') guards SAMPLED outputs against exactly that selection pressure, and an empty string is not a sampled output. The residual risk, that empties correlate with hard queries, is unchanged in direction and strictly smaller in size than the status quo, which does not retry those cells but DELETES them.
